<warning>Printed woodblock Buddhist sutra in vertical traditional Mongolian script with red ink (Kanjur format) and marginal Chinese volume/folio notation. The main Mongolian text is not reliably transcribable and is marked with unclear tags.</warning>

<margin>Eighth section, one hundred and fifty <note>original: "naimadugar bölüg зуун тавин"; Mongolian marginal notation indicating the section and folio number 150</note></margin>

<unclear>28 vertical lines of Classical Mongolian script printed in red ink, not transcribed</unclear>

<margin>Secret Sutra, Volume Five, Part One, One Hundred and Fifty <note>original: "秘密經第五卷上一百五十"; Chinese woodblock marginal notation identifying the tantric section, fifth fascicle, upper part, folio 150</note></margin>

<summary>This folio comes from a woodblock edition of the Mongolian Kanjur printed in red ink. The marginal notations in both Mongolian and Chinese identify it as folio 150 of the eighth section (Chinese: Secret Sutra, Volume 5, Part 1), while the 28 vertical lines of the main Classical Mongolian text remain untranscribed.</summary>
<keywords>Mongolian Kanjur, Secret Sutra, Buddhist sutra, woodblock print, Classical Mongolian script, folio 150, bilingual marginalia</keywords>
